points.description: Classification defined as mapping data/inputs to discrete labels (classes or categories).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'sorting into groups') without 'discrete' or labels/classes.

points.description: Regression defined as mapping data/inputs to continuous values (real-valued outputs or a continuous function).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'predicts numbers') without 'continuous' or real values.

points.description: States the difference in output type: discrete labels for classification versus continuous/real values for regression, as an explicit contrast.
points.partial_credit: Half if the contrast is only implied by the two definitions or is vague.

points.description: Error measure differs: classification error is the number of misclassifications; regression error is the summed distance (e.g. sum of differences/squared errors) between true and predicted values.
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of the two error measures is correct or both are vague.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both tasks correctly defined (discrete labels vs continuous/real values), the contrast made clear, and the differing error measures given. Award part marks for vague wording or for giving only one error measure. Give no marks for a swapped or wrong definition; each point is judged on its own.
